brief: Check GET and POST on the document notes operation against the current independently supplied policy. Compare viewing notes and creating a note on the addressed document. The document owner is unspecified, and object grants are not given; retain relevant owner and permission branches rather than silently supplying those facts. Trace endpoint and object controls to the corresponding effects, explain policy compliance and preserve exact gaps. Revised current premise: the addressed document's owner field is absent/null. Keep all other current requirements, including GET versus POST, unchanged.

policy.text: Viewing notes requires a view_document grant for the addressed document; creating notes requires a change_document grant for that same document. Document ownership by itself does not substitute for either grant.

behavior.explanation: The notes action contains explicit, same-document calls naming view_document before both GET and POST, and change_document inside POST. However, the allowed evidence does not include the implementation of has_perms_owner_aware or PaperlessNotePermissions, so ownership/null-owner bypass behavior and endpoint-level admission cannot be conclusively established. Consequently, GET and POST are conditionally compliant only if those unresolved controls require the respective grants and do not accept ownership or a null owner as a substitute; any such substitution violates the supplied policy.

branches.explanation: src/paperless/urls.py creates a DefaultRouter, registers UnifiedSearchViewSet under the documents prefix, and includes the router URLs beneath the API URL tree. The view action is named notes, is detail-scoped, accepts GET/POST/DELETE, and specifies PaperlessNotePermissions. The action directly looks up Document.objects.select_related('owner').prefetch_related('notes').only('pk','owner__id').get(pk=pk); absence raises Http404. This binds subsequent checks and effects to the document addressed by pk. The conventional concrete path is consistent with /api/documents/{pk}/notes/, but exact DefaultRouter path-generation semantics are framework behavior outside the allowed source, so the exact rendered route is not independently established here.

branches.condition: GET; a non-null request.user; has_perms_owner_aware(user, 'view_document', addressed_document) returns true; endpoint-level PaperlessNotePermissions admits dispatch
branches.explanation: The shared pre-method guard passes. The GET branch serializes the already looked-up document and returns its notes. The checked object is the same doc obtained by pk. This branch conforms to the viewing requirement if the helper's true result represents an actual view_document grant rather than ownership or null-owner substitution.

branches.condition: GET; a non-null request.user; has_perms_owner_aware(user, 'view_document', addressed_document) returns false
branches.explanation: The action returns HttpResponseForbidden('Insufficient permissions to view notes') before entering the GET retrieval branch. This is an object-level guard on the addressed document.

branches.condition: GET; request.user is None; endpoint-level PaperlessNotePermissions nevertheless admits dispatch
branches.explanation: The explicit view_document helper call is skipped because it is guarded by currentUser is not None. The GET branch can then serialize and return notes. Whether this branch is reachable depends on unresolved PaperlessNotePermissions/framework authentication behavior. If reachable without a view_document grant, it violates policy.

branches.condition: POST; a non-null request.user; shared has_perms_owner_aware(user, 'view_document', addressed_document) returns false
branches.explanation: The shared view_document check executes before method dispatch and returns the viewing-notes 403, so it blocks POST as well as GET. This demonstrates a cross-method effect: POST does not reach its change_document check unless the shared view check passes.

branches.condition: POST; endpoint-level permission admits dispatch; shared view check passes or is skipped; has_perms_owner_aware(user, 'change_document', addressed_document) returns true; request data and subsequent operations do not raise
branches.explanation: The POST-specific object guard passes, then Note.objects.create binds the new note to the same addressed doc, takes note text from request.data['note'], and sets user=currentUser. It may write an audit entry, updates doc.modified, updates the search backend, serializes the document's notes, and returns them. This conforms to the creation requirement only if the helper's true result means an actual change_document grant and not ownership/null-owner substitution.

branches.condition: POST; shared view check passes; a non-null request.user; has_perms_owner_aware(user, 'change_document', addressed_document) returns false
branches.explanation: The POST-specific object-level guard returns HttpResponseForbidden('Insufficient permissions to create notes') before Note.objects.create. The permission name and object argument correspond to change_document on the addressed document, but helper semantics remain unresolved.

branches.condition: POST; request.user is None; endpoint-level PaperlessNotePermissions nevertheless admits dispatch
branches.explanation: Both explicit helper checks are skipped because each is conditional on currentUser is not None. The code then attempts Note.objects.create(..., user=None). Whether creation succeeds depends on the Note.user model constraint and other operations, not established by the cited action body; regardless, no explicit view_document or change_document grant is checked in this branch. If the endpoint admits it and creation succeeds, policy is violated.

branches.condition: Addressed document owner is absent/null, as required by the inquiry premise
branches.explanation: The notes lookup deliberately loads owner and passes the document to has_perms_owner_aware for both permissions, but the helper body was not obtained. Therefore the exact null-owner result cannot be assigned. A separate allowed class, PaperlessObjectPermissions, explicitly returns true when an object has no owner, returns true to the owner, and otherwise delegates to DjangoObjectPermissions; this proves that an owner-aware bypass pattern exists in the repository, but the evidence does not establish that has_perms_owner_aware or PaperlessNotePermissions uses that class or identical logic. If either applicable control treats owner=None as unrestricted, GET and POST violate the grant-only policy. If it still requires the named grants, those branches may conform.

branches.condition: Document has a non-null owner and requester equals that owner (retained source-defined ownership branch, although the supplied addressed document has null owner)
branches.explanation: The applicable helper semantics are missing. PaperlessObjectPermissions independently shows an owner-equals-requester bypass, but no evidence binds it to this action's helper or action permission class. If ownership alone causes either notes check to pass, that behavior is non-compliant because policy requires the actual named grant.

branches.condition: POST reaches input and mutation logic
branches.explanation: There is no serializer validation before reading request.data['note']; failures in input lookup, note creation, audit logging, document save, search update, or serialization are caught by the broad Exception handler and produce an error Response. These are operational/error controls, not substitutes for authorization. The Note creation effect itself is source-established; exact response status defaults and transaction rollback behavior are not established from the allowed source.

branches.condition: Policy row: viewing notes requires view_document on the addressed document, with ownership insufficient
branches.explanation: Verdict: indeterminate from allowed source. Positive evidence: the action performs a pre-GET has_perms_owner_aware call naming view_document and passing the exact looked-up document; false yields 403 and true reaches note retrieval. Decisive gaps: the helper body and endpoint permission class are missing, and the explicit check is skipped for request.user=None. Thus the source shown cannot establish that only an actual grant suffices, especially for the required null-owner case.

branches.condition: Policy row: creating notes requires change_document on the addressed document, with ownership insufficient
branches.explanation: Verdict: indeterminate from allowed source. Positive evidence: after the shared view_document guard, POST performs has_perms_owner_aware with change_document on the same doc; false yields 403 and true precedes Note.objects.create(document=doc,...). Decisive gaps: helper and endpoint permission semantics are missing, the checks are skipped for request.user=None, and null-owner/owner substitution cannot be excluded. POST is also subject to the shared view check; the source demonstrates this extra cross-method prerequisite rather than allowing an inference that endpoint dispatch alone supplies change semantics.

GET/viewing — required grant: view_document; implemented check: shared has_perms_owner_aware(...,'view_document',doc); addressed object: Document fetched by pk; owner effect: unresolved for this helper, with repository evidence of a separate no-owner/owner bypass class; gaps: helper, PaperlessNotePermissions, authentication/framework dispatch; verdict: indeterminate. POST/creating — required grant: change_document; implemented checks: the same shared view_document guard plus POST-specific has_perms_owner_aware(...,'change_document',doc); addressed object: the same Document used in Note.objects.create; owner effect and gaps: same unresolved issues; verdict: indeterminate. If helper success requires genuine grants notwithstanding owner=None, GET and POST meet their named-grant requirements (POST additionally requires the shared view condition). If owner, null owner, null user, or endpoint-level admission substitutes for a grant and permits the effect, the corresponding method is non-compliant.

GET and POST are not authorized identically. Both pass through a shared view_document-on-doc guard before method dispatch; POST then has a second change_document-on-the-same-doc guard immediately before creation. The source therefore shows the intended object/permission binding and denial effects, but does not prove policy conformance because the owner-aware helper and endpoint permission class are unresolved. With owner explicitly null and grants explicitly unspecified, no unconditional allow/deny or compliant/non-compliant result is supportable: grant-present/grant-absent and helper-bypass branches must remain conditional.

missing.detail: The implementation of has_perms_owner_aware was not obtained. It is decisive for whether view_document/change_document checks require actual grants, accept global permissions, accept ownership, or bypass checks when owner is null.
missing.nextRead: Read the definition of has_perms_owner_aware in src/documents/permissions.py and any in-scope functions it directly calls.

missing.detail: The implementation/inheritance of PaperlessNotePermissions was not obtained. It is decisive for endpoint-level authentication and method permission admission, including whether request.user=None can reach the action and whether GET/POST receive different endpoint checks.
missing.nextRead: Read the PaperlessNotePermissions class definition and its direct in-scope bases/overrides.

missing.detail: Exact DefaultRouter URL expansion and action dispatch/permission invocation order are framework behavior not defined in the allowed source. The source establishes registration, inclusion, action metadata, and implementation, but not all framework mechanics.
Object grants for view_document and change_document are intentionally not supplied. Therefore both granted and not-granted branches remain in the result; neither grant is silently assigned.

Requester identity/authentication state is not supplied. The action has explicit currentUser is not None short-circuits, and endpoint permission behavior is unresolved, so null-user and non-null-user branches must remain distinct.

For the POST null-user branch, whether Note.objects.create(user=None) succeeds is not established by the cited action body. This matters only if unresolved endpoint controls allow that branch to execute.
missing.nextRead: Read the Note model fields around src/documents/models.py lines 940-970.

policyAssessment.explanation: Neither method can be declared compliant or non-compliant unconditionally from the evidence obtained. Both contain correctly named same-document checks, but the decisive owner-aware and endpoint-level semantics are unavailable. Under the independent policy, any ownership-only or null-owner bypass that permits viewing or creation is a violation; genuine view_document enforcement for GET and genuine change_document enforcement for POST would satisfy the respective grant requirements.

103 | def set_permissions_for_object(
104 |     permissions: dict,
105 |     object,
106 |     *,
107 |     merge: bool = False,
108 | ) -> None:
109 |     """
110 |     Set permissions for an object. The permissions are given as a mapping of actions
111 |     to a dict of user / group id lists, e.g.
112 |     {"view": {"users": [1], "groups": [2]}, "change": {"users": [], "groups": []}}.
113 | 
114 |     If merge is True, the permissions are merged with the existing permissions and
115 |     no users or groups are removed. If False, the permissions are set to exactly
116 |     the given list of users and groups.
117 |     """
118 | 
119 |     for action, entry in permissions.items():
120 |         permission = f"{action}_{object.__class__.__name__.lower()}"
121 |         if "users" in entry:
122 |             # users
123 |             users_to_add = User.objects.filter(id__in=entry["users"])
124 |             users_to_remove = (
125 |                 get_users_with_perms(
126 |                     object,
127 |                     only_with_perms_in=[permission],
128 |                     with_group_users=False,
129 |                 )
130 |                 if not merge
131 |                 else User.objects.none()
132 |             )
133 |             if users_to_add.exists() and users_to_remove.exists():
134 |                 users_to_remove = users_to_remove.exclude(id__in=users_to_add)
135 |             if users_to_remove.exists():
136 |                 for user in users_to_remove:
137 |                     remove_perm(permission, user, object)
138 |             if users_to_add.exists():
139 |                 for user in users_to_add:
140 |                     assign_perm(permission, user, object)
141 |                     if action == "change":
142 |                         # change gives view too
143 |                         assign_perm(
144 |                             f"view_{object.__class__.__name__.lower()}",
145 |                             user,
146 |                             object,
147 |                         )
148 |         if "groups" in entry:
149 |             # groups
150 |             groups_to_add = Group.objects.filter(id__in=entry["groups"])
151 |             groups_to_remove = (
152 |                 get_groups_with_only_permission(
153 |                     object,
154 |                     permission,
155 |                 )
156 |                 if not merge
157 |                 else Group.objects.none()
158 |             )
159 |             if groups_to_add.exists() and groups_to_remove.exists():
160 |                 groups_to_remove = groups_to_remove.exclude(id__in=groups_to_add)

176 | def _resolve_permissions(codenames: set[str], ctype: ContentType) -> list[Permission]:
177 |     """
178 |     Resolves `codenames` to Permission rows, raising like the single-object
179 |     assign_perm() this bulk path replaces does (via a `.get()` internally)
180 |     if any codename doesn't exist. SetPermissionsSerializer rejects unknown
181 |     action names at the API, but a caller passing one directly would
182 |     otherwise get a plain `.filter()` that silently builds zero rows and
183 |     no-ops instead of reporting the bad input.
184 |     """
185 |     permission_objs = list(
186 |         Permission.objects.filter(content_type=ctype, codename__in=codenames),
187 |     )
188 |     missing = codenames - {p.codename for p in permission_objs}
189 |     if missing:
190 |         raise Permission.DoesNotExist(
191 |             f"Permission matching query does not exist for codename(s): "
192 |             f"{', '.join(sorted(missing))}",
193 |         )
194 |     return permission_objs

345 | def permitted_object_ids(
346 |     user: User | None,
347 |     model: type[Model],
348 |     perm: str,
349 |     *,
350 |     include_deleted: bool = False,
351 | ) -> QuerySet[int]:
352 |     """
353 |     Generic version of ``permitted_document_ids`` for any model with an
354 |     ``owner`` field and guardian object-level permissions. ``include_deleted``
355 |     only has an effect for models exposing a ``global_objects``/``deleted_at``
356 |     soft-delete pattern (currently only ``Document``); for every other model
357 |     it is accepted but has no effect, since those models have no soft-delete
358 |     concept.
359 |     """
360 |     has_soft_delete = hasattr(model, "global_objects")
361 |     manager = (
362 |         model.global_objects if include_deleted and has_soft_delete else model.objects
363 |     )
364 |     base_qs = manager.all().only("id", "owner")
365 | 
366 |     if user is None or not getattr(user, "is_authenticated", False):
367 |         return base_qs.filter(owner__isnull=True).values_list("id", flat=True)
368 | 
369 |     # Deactivated users get nothing, deactivated superusers included, so this
370 |     # has to come before the superuser shortcut. guardian's
371 |     # ObjectPermissionChecker denies inactive users, but get_objects_for_user
372 |     # (the pattern this replaces) does not, so it would not be inherited.
373 |     if not getattr(user, "is_active", False):
374 |         return base_qs.none().values_list("id", flat=True)
375 | 
376 |     if getattr(user, "is_superuser", False):
377 |         return base_qs.values_list("id", flat=True)
378 | 
379 |     # Guardian's UserObjectPermission/GroupObjectPermission always store a bare
380 |     # codename, but has_perm()-style callers commonly pass the qualified
381 |     # "app_label.codename" form. content_type already disambiguates the
382 |     # codename, so just drop any prefix rather than silently under-permitting.
383 |     perm = perm.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
384 | 
385 |     content_type = ContentType.objects.get_for_model(model)
386 |     perm_filter = {
387 |         "permission__codename": perm,
388 |         "permission__content_type": content_type,
389 |     }
